items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains the lowest of men
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching rightfully be given?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
It is the fifth chapter
items.inference: The fifth chapter of the text emerged from Candradvīpa concludes here.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of Kaula been known?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The Kaula determination is now known
items.inference: The speaker has come to know the Kaula determination through the lord of Kaulas' grace.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The speaker asks to be told fully into what the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality being described?
premises: The subject is identified as supreme
It is partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The ultimate reality is supreme, partless, eternal, and untouched by affliction or impurity.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in relation to haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also called the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.
uncertainties: The exact sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is doctrinally compressed.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
It is described as situated
Its location is in all beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The subject is the same soul
The condition is merely leaving the body
It is then designated supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and received according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes down through tradition
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This teaching is received aurally as something transmitted through an unbroken tradition.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the traditional lineage.

items.question: What effect is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The means is mere knowledge
That knowledge is heard
The fair-faced goddess is addressed
items.inference: Even merely hearing this knowledge is presented as having significant efficacy.
uncertainties: The sentence is syntactically incomplete and continues into the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, when it is heard...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads toward freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner is described as one who practices
The state aimed at is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state associated with renunciation and freedom from bondage.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of kāṣāyaṃ is ambiguous in this compressed construction.
items.plain_english: If one practices for six months, taking up the ochre robe and becoming free from bondage...

items.question: What twofold result follows from the prescribed yogic practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
Union with them is attained
items.inference: The practice results in freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: He becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī
A teaching has been told to her
That teaching concerns the practice of the soul
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been communicated to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: What qualities qualify a recipient to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one who is fully endowed and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The case shift between genitive and locative is unusual in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: Why must the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
Its origin is from the yoginīs
It is explicitly not to be given
items.inference: The Kaula essence, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given out.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to sāraṃ is compressed.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after removal of ignorance's veil?
premises: The speaker refers to her own body
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now declared pure
items.inference: The speaker claims her body, once veiled by ignorance, is now pure.
uncertainties: The case of deham is unexpected given the predicate nirmalaṃ.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time is now sought?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish to hear
The topic concerns time
The sought teaching is the auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious method for deceiving time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the possibility of destroying death?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
Death can be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching will explain without doubt how death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: What paradoxical condition affects even the wise at the source of nectar?
premises: The context involves the tip of nectar
There is burning by the essence of juice
Even the wise are affected
items.inference: Even a wise person can be burned at the source of nectar by its potent essence.
uncertainties: The imagery of burning at the tip of nectar is obscure and may be technical.
items.plain_english: Even the wise person is burned at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic technique involving breath at the palate is prescribed?
premises: The locus is the root of tongue and palate
An action is performed there
One should slowly drink the air
items.inference: The practitioner should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing oneself at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When this practice is maintained for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for one established in this practice?
premises: The body may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
Poison does not enter the body
items.inference: For such a practitioner, even the venom of great serpents does not enter the body.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
